vetSays.line: ⚠ This one is different — old, patient, unhurried — it has seen your kind before. An Elder veteran.
Vsevolod strikes the Elder The Mountain Lord.
The Elder The Mountain Lord falls.
📺 +20 style — dropped the Elder The Mountain Lord!
🛡️ Noah, Franz, Hassan, Owen and Emma met them at the door — 5 put down. Noah, Franz, Hassan, Owen, Emma are hurt.

📺 "Oh, you survived the AUDIENCE NOTES? Cute. We've stopped pretending these are animals now. That was the FINAL DRAFT, folks — what comes out of the treeline next was never alive the way you mean it."

📺 "We've been watching you for a LONG time. Your faiths. Your formats. Your little institutions. So we built something out of... well. Out of YOU. Say hello to the MIRROR DRAFT."

◈ SYSTEM: "Four waves. FOUR. The producers are — okay, I'm saying it: FINALES need a NATION. You've got a region; now make it a REALM. Bind fires under one head, or bend the knee to someone who has. The higher-ups are watching. ...Did I say higher-ups? I said NOTHING. Forget the higher-ups."

◈ ARC IV — THE INEFFICIENCY. SYSTEM: "ROUNDING ERROR RECLASSIFIED: ANOMALY. Organic consumption yields impossible output. Recalculating. Recalculating." — They finally see it. The thing they laughed at — needing to EAT — is the engine. Their confusion is your weapon now. You stood up to the calibration fauna, the audience's notes, the Final Draft — lived through their Show, weathered the worst together, and built something bigger than a village. One day humanity will need a case to make. The case is made of deeds, not words — and yours, though unfinished, are undeniable. (Feasted buffs burn ho
📺 "But finales — FINALES need a LEGEND, sweetheart. More STANDING — blood, bonds, or bread — and look the Mirror Draft in the eye. The producers are WAITING."
📺 SYSTEM: "Oh — OH. Everybody saw that, right? Vsevolod just put down Buffering... on CAMERA. That's a veteran kill, folks. REMEMBER the name."

opens.openerLine: "Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"Hey." Emmett settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to."
"About what you think happened to us — I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"Please — have you got anything to spare? Anything? I can't keep going like this."
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"I mean — Back home I was a musician. The skills don't transfer, but the stubbornness does."
"Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"Please — do you have anything to eat? Anything at all? I can't keep going like this."
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"About teaching them something — Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"About what you make of all this — What do you make of all this? Really."
"I had a whole conversation in my head just now. It went well. Your turn."
"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Practical view: I used to need noise to sleep. Now I need silence and I can't find enough of it."
"Mind if I just sit with you for a bit?"
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the meadow edge, west of the creek."
"About that warning — I keep turning it over."
"The pantry run — I haven't stopped thinking about it."
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"Hey. Got a minute? No reason. Just — hey."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. Good talking."
"About the pantry run — still on my mind. I keep coming back to it."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I froze when it mattered. I think about it every day."
I don't pick sides. I pick the group. Every time.
"Can I tell you something? At night I count the stars and name them after people."
Someday kids will sit by a fire and hear what I did. I want it to be a good one.
"Have you heard? No? Good, I get to tell you first."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
"I'm sorry — whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. I need help. Please."
"About where you're from — Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
"About that news I was bursting to share — You'll never guess what I saw by the treeline. What could go wrong."
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Okay, so — something happened this morning."
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
Nobody goes hungry on my watch. That's the whole plan. Everything else is details.
"You'll never guess what I saw by the treeline. I don't know, though."
"About that news I was bursting to share — Have you heard? No? Good, I get to tell you first."
"About what's on my mind — I keep turning it over."
"About that warning — I keep turning it over. Worth considering."
Hold it together. That's my whole philosophy. Hold it together.
"About that news I was bursting to share — Okay, so — something happened this morning."
"You'll never guess what I saw by the treeline."
"The snare line's a mess — wind took half of it. Tomorrow, you and me, re-tying? An hour's work for two."
"I need company tonight — not talking, just... near. I don't want to be alone when the light goes."
"I asked Miles about that news I was bursting to share — Miles's gone. Have you heard? No? Good, I get to tell you first."
"Funny thing: Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"We're down to 2 liters of clean water. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"Can I tell you something? I know who took the extra rations but won't say."

"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. We're down to 4 liters of clean water. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"About that news I was bursting to share — You'll never guess what I saw by the treeline. That's the whole of it."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. Can you — would you stay close tonight? I don't want to be alone when it gets dark."
"Never mind the snare line — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I hate to ask, but tell me you've got food to spare. I'm going hungry here. I can't keep going like this."
"Never mind staying close tonight — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I'm sorry — whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"About the help I asked you for — That night has passed. Let’s leave that request behind."
"I asked Hassan about the creek water run — Hassan's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"About the creek water run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"I don't know what to do with my hands today."
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Have you — sorry. I keep thinking about them."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet. Could be wrong, though."
"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"We need to — Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan. Let's move."
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"About the most useful thing you've learned — What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"Please — tell me you've got food to spare. I'm going hungry here. I can't keep going like this."
"What if — just what if — the monsters aren't the problem?"
"Hey. Got a minute? No reason. Just — hey."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"I mean this — ...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"I asked Thuli about the pantry run — Thuli's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
You two sort it out, or I will, and nobody likes my version.

lines.line: (Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
...and then it lands: A man, maybe 50s speaks 🇺🇸 English. A few shared words. Gestures. Patience.
"Miguel," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Miguel." You'll remember that.
